summary: schema present; generated defines it at components.schemas.PatchItem, components.PatchItem; 1 extra

answer.why_different: The generated side places an additional copy of the schema at `components.PatchItem`, rather than only under the valid reusable-schema map `components.schemas`. This is a different address/placement, not a different PatchItem structure. The extra key is not a permitted fixed field of the OpenAPI Components Object and is therefore an invalid OpenAPI 3.0 placement.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP specification defines PatchItem as a data type with the fields `op`, `from`, `path`, and `value`; it does not support adding a second top-level components entry. S6 states that `from` and `value` are part of the PatchItem type, and S13 identifies PatchItem as a defined data type.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI 3.0 defines reusable schemas under `components.schemas`; the Components Object has fixed fields such as `schemas` and permits only specification extensions beyond those fields. `components.PatchItem` is therefore not a valid location for a schema and makes the generated document invalid.
answer.clearer_why: The official version has one unambiguous, valid definition at `components.schemas.PatchItem`. The generated version duplicates the definition and adds an invalid sibling location, which can confuse readers and cannot be reliably interpreted by OpenAPI tooling.

evidence.title: 12.1.3.2.5 Notification notifyMOIChanges
evidence.text:
JSON Patch, attribute elements are identified based on their index, i.e.
based on the position in the array.  
\- In case no key is defined for a YANG \"list\" it is not possible to
report the creation, deletion or replacement of individual list entries.
In this case, whenever the list is modified, the replacement of the
complete attribute or attribute field (the complete list with all list
enties) shall be reported.  
\- Similarly if an attribute(field) is mapped to a YANG leaf-list with
non-unique values it is not possible to report the creation, deletion or
replacement of an individual value. In this case, whenever the leaf-list
is modified, the replacement of the complete attribute or attribute
field (the complete leaf-list; all values) shall be reported.  
\- YANG default values shall be handled as follows:  
\- Attributes with default values, for which no value is specified in
the object creation request, shall be included in the object creation
report with their default values.  
\- Attributes with default values, that are deleted and consequently set
to their default value, shall be included in attribute replacement
reports.

evidence.query: reusable schemas held in components schemas, $ref PatchItem
evidence.text:
```
MyResponseType:
oneOf:
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cat'
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Lizard'
discriminator:
propertyName: pet_type
```  
The expectation now is that a property with name `pet_type` _MUST_ be present in the response payload, and the value will correspond to the name of a schema defined in the OAS document.  Thus the response payload:  
```
{
"id": 12345,
"pet_type": "Cat"
}
```  
Will indicate that the `Cat` schema be used in conjunction with this payload.  
In scenarios where the value of the discriminator field does not match the schema name or implicit mapping is not possible, an optional `mapping` definition MAY be used:  
```
MyResponseType:
oneOf:
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cat'
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Lizard'
- $ref: 'https://gigantic-server.com/schemas/Monster/schema.json'
discriminator:
propertyName: pet_type
mapping:
dog: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
```  
